core_principles.text: Utilize a controlled tempo, specifically performing controlled eccentrics lasting 2 to 3 seconds.
Perform exercises through a full range of motion rather than rushing through partial repetitions.

common_mistakes.text: Rushing through repetitions and performing partial range of motion reps.

specific_findings.text: A tempo utilizing controlled eccentrics of 2 to 3 seconds is recommended to maximize hypertrophy compared to rushed partial reps.

core_principles.text: Perform hammer curls with a neutral grip where the palms face towards each other.
Utilize a supinated forearm position to maximize the power of the biceps brachii as an elbow flexor.

common_mistakes.text: Allowing the elbows to pull forward when performing curls.

specific_findings.text: The brachialis is the primary flexor of the elbow, generating 50-60% of the force.

consequences.text: Because the biceps brachii is a biarticular muscle responsible for both elbow flexion and shoulder stabilization, it can cause the elbows to pull forward during curls.
Performing curls in a supinated position can place significantly greater tension on the elbow's tendons compared to a neutral grip.

core_principles.text: Tuck your elbows so that they are flush against your body and near the waist, keeping them in the same position during the entire range of motion.
Bring the implement as far up as you are able to, maximizing the range of motion.
Let the weight down in a slow and controlled manner.
Minimize any amount of body movement and keep the body as still as possible during the entire exercise.

common_mistakes.text: Exhibiting excessive body swaying to get the weight up.
Allowing the elbows to move from their stationary position near the waist during the curl.

specific_findings.text: The biceps contribute the most to flexion when the hands are in a supinated position.
Studies have shown the eccentric portion of a movement has been found to be more responsible for muscle damage and thereby can elicit greater growth gains.
Bicep curls should be programmed for hypertrophy using a moderate weight that allows for 8-12 reps.

consequences.text: Using a supinated grip puts the wrist in a more compromising position compared to a neutral grip, making it more difficult to maintain correct form under heavy loads.
Performing standard bicep curls instead of hammer curls can lead to discomfort in the elbow due to the biomechanical positioning of the joints.
